target_customer: Individual desktop users and small businesses who needed to search files and email on their own computer
problem: Finding files, email and documents on a personal computer was slow with the built-in tools of the time.

founders.name: Zak Stone
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. An aggregator names Chris Slowe as co-founder and says Stone later became a Google product manager; both are unverified.

competitors.name: Google Desktop Search
competitors.traction_then: Final release in March 2005, moved to enterprise by May 2005

competitors.name: Yahoo Desktop Search (X1 technology)
competitors.what: Free desktop search built on X1 technology

competitors.name: Copernic Desktop Search
competitors.traction_then: Ranked top overall in an April 2005 university benchmark

competitors.name: Apple Spotlight
competitors.what: Search built into the operating system
competitors.traction_then: Shipped with OS X Tiger in April 2005

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing local files and email across formats is standard systems engineering with some hard parts, doable by a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Free products from Google, Yahoo, Microsoft and Apple, plus Copernic and X1, were launching in the same months, so a standalone desktop search tool was easy to match.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Between late 2004 and April 2005 the large platform companies each shipped free desktop search, which absorbed the category.

market_need_then: Desktop search was a hot topic in 2004 to 2005 with trade coverage of the race, but a 2004 trade piece asked who cares, so willingness to pay for it was unclear.

branding.domain_note: memamp.com is now a parked domain listed for sale on GoDaddy (checked 2026).

brand_strength.rationale: No press, logo or community evidence about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Memamp was a Summer 2005 YC desktop search company that is now inactive and whose domain is parked for sale. The cause of shutdown is not public; no post-mortem or founder account was found. One unverified aggregator blames competition from Spotlight and Google Desktop, which is plausible given that Google, Yahoo, Microsoft and Apple all shipped free desktop search within months of its batch, but it is not confirmed.
notes: CB Insights lists a single seed round dated 2005-06 with Y Combinator and no amount, which is the standard YC deal, so not recorded as a round. Competitor traction comes from general market coverage, not from Memamp specific sources. Shutdown date unknown. Cause suggestion from startupintros is unverified. name_problems value is free text and may need adjustment.
